stories-34-15-19-saba-two-gardens-flood-.title: Two Gardens of Sheba Swept Away by the Flood of the Marib Dam
stories-34-15-19-saba-two-gardens-flood-.note: Surah 34:15–19 recounts how Sheba's two irrigated gardens on the right and left were swept away by the Flood of the Dam (Sayl al-'Arim), corresponding to the South Arabian Marib Dam breaches celebrated in pre-Islamic poetry preserved in al-Tabari.

discussion.view: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite South Arabian genealogists and pre-Islamic poets such as al-A'sha to identify al-'Arim as the great stone dam of Ma'rib built by Himyar and Saba', whose breach scattered the Sabaean tribes across Arabia.
discussion.reply: Epigraphic South Arabian inscriptions at Ma'rib (such as CIH 540 and CIH 541 from the fifth and sixth centuries AD) and pre-Islamic verses by al-A'sha document repeated breaches of the Ma'rib irrigation dam that turned its flanking oases into desert scrub, situating 34:15–19 in local Arabian historical memory.

stories-34-15-19-saba-two-gardens-flood-.quranEn: [15] Certainly for Sheba there was a sign in their dwelling place – two gardens, on the right and left: ‘Eat from the provision of your Lord, and be thankful to Him. A good land and a forgiving Lord.’ [16] But they turned away, so We sent on them the flood of ‘Arim, and We replaced for them their two gardens (with) two gardens producing bitter fruit, and tamarisks, and a few lote trees. [17] We repaid them that because they disbelieved. We do not repay (anyone) but the ungrateful? [18] We set between them and the towns which We have blessed (other) towns (which are still) visible, and We measured out the traveling (distance) between them: ‘Travel among them by night and day in security!’ [19] But they said, ‘Our Lord, lengthen (the distance) between our journeys.’ They did themselves evil, so We made them legendary, and We tore them completely to pieces. Surely in that are signs indeed for every patient (and) thankful one.
quranHighlights: Certainly for Sheba there was a sign in their dwelling place – two gardens, on the right and left
so We sent on them the flood of ‘Arim, and We replaced for them their two gardens

sources.workSub: Jami' al-Bayan (Tafsir al-Tabari — Pre-Islamic Arabian Historical & Poetic Witness)
sources.date: 9th–10th century AD (preserving pre-Islamic Arabian poetry and reports)
sources.en: And Al-‘Arim is the dam (Al-Musannah) that holds back the water, the singular of which is ‘aramah. This is what Al-A‘sha meant by his saying: 'Therein is an example for the one who seeks consolation And Ma'rib, which Al-‘Arim has effaced. A dam of large stones that Himyar built for them When their water came, it did not flow away.'
highlights: And Al-‘Arim is the dam (Al-Musannah) that holds back the water
And Ma'rib, which Al-‘Arim has effaced.
A dam of large stones that Himyar built for them
sources.orig: والعرم المسناة التي تحبس الماء، واحدها عرمة، وإياه عنى الأعشى بقوله: فَفِـــي ذَاكَ للْمُؤْتَسِـــي أُسْــوَةٌ وَمَــأْرِبُ عَفَّــى عليــه العَــرِمْ رِجـــامٌ بَنَتْـــهُ لَهُــمْ حِــمْيَرٌ إذا جَـــاءَ مــاؤهُمُ لــمْ يَــرمْ
